A function to read the experimental data:

```{r}
reading_exp_data <- function(file) {
  hours <- c(0, 5, 48, 72)
  days <- c(5, 7, 14, 28)
  hash <- c(setNames(hours, paste0("H", hours)),
            setNames(24 * days, paste0("D", days)))
  
  file |> 
    read_rds2() |> 
    filter(treatment == "AL+AP") |> 
    mutate(t = hash[stringr::str_remove(time_points, "0")],
           value = Inhibition / 100) |> 
    select(t, value)
}
```

Stratified bootstrapping:

```{r}
stratified_bootstrap <- function(df, N) {
  map(1:ceiling(N), ~ df |> 
                        group_by(t) |> 
                        group_split() |> 
                        map(slice_sample, prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |> 
                        bind_rows())
}
```

```{r}
predict_glm <- function(object, newdata, ci = .95) {
  q_val <- qt(1 - (1 - ci) / 2, object$df.residual)
  f <- object$family$linkinv
  newdata <- as_tibble(newdata)
  newdata |> 
    bind_cols(head(predict(object, newdata, se.fit = TRUE), -1)) |> 
    mutate(lwr = f(fit - q_val * se.fit),
           upr = f(fit + q_val * se.fit),
           fit = f(fit)) |> 
    select(-se.fit)
}
```

## Theoretical model

### Parasite load and infectiousness

#### 1 bite, all human treated

Call $t$ the **time post drug administration** in treated humans and $\tau$ the
**time post mosquito infection**. Call $\alpha(t, \tau)$ the
**transmission blocking activity** (TBA) defined as the percentage reduction of the
number of mosquitoes infected consecutively to 1 blood meal at times $t$ and $\tau$.
Call $\beta(t, \tau)$ the **transmission reducing activity** (TRA) defined as the
percentage reduction of the parasite load in infected mosquitoes consecutively to 1
blood meal at times $t$ and $\tau$. The mean reduction factor of the parasite load due
to TBA and TRA and across the population of infected mosquitoes at times $t$ and $\tau$
then reads

$$
(1 - \alpha(t, \tau))(1 - \beta(t, \tau)).
$$

Call $h(t)$ is the density of probability of the
**distribution of times post drug administration** in the population of treated humans.
The mean reduction factor $l(\tau, m)$ of parasite load across the population of
infected mosquitoes due to **1 bite on treated people at time $\tau$** then reads

$$
l(\tau, m) = \int_0^{m}(1 - \alpha(t, \tau))(1 - \beta(t, \tau))h(t)dt.
$$

when we consider people who have been infected over the past $m$ hours. Whenever we
would need $m = +\infty$ in theory, a value of $m$ large enough so that
$\alpha(t,\tau) = \beta(t,\tau)\simeq 0$ would be enough in practice.

#### Multiple bites, $p\%$ human treated

Call $a$ the **mosquito bite rate**, $p(m)$ the
**proportion of the human population that has received treatment** over the past $m$
hours and $\lambda(\tau,m)$ the
**mean cumulative reduction factor of the parasite load due to all the bites that have occurred until time $\tau$**.
The fact that each bite on a treated human reduces the parasite load of
$(1 - l(\tau,m)) \%$ is conveyed by the following differential equation

$$
\frac{d\lambda}{d\tau} = -(1 - l(\tau, m)) a p(m) \lambda(\tau, m).
$$

If we now assume that mosquitoes get infected by bites on untreated humans only then

$$
\lambda(0, m) = 1,
$$

which leads to the following expression of the mean cumulative reduction factor of the
parasite load at time $\tau$

$$
\lambda(\tau, m) = \exp\left[-ap(m)\int_0^\tau(1 - l(u,m))du\right]
$$

#### Mean infectiousness reduction

Call $\zeta(\lambda)$ the function that converts a **reduction factor of parasite load**
$\lambda$ into a **reduction factor of mosquito infectiousness** and $\mu$ the
**mosquito death rate** assumed to be independent of the mosquito's age. The mean
reduction factor of mosquito infectiousness in the total mosquito population due to TBA
and TRA can then be expressed as

$$
\theta = \int_0^{+\infty}\mu e^{-\mu\tau}\zeta(\lambda(\tau,m))d\tau.
$$

### Parasite maturation and EIP

Call $z(\tau)$ the **proportion of infectious mosquitoes** at time $\tau$ post
infection and assume it increases logistically from some arbitrary value close to 0
right after infection to 1 when all the mosquitoes are infectious. Under the same
assumption as above that mosquitoes get infected by bites on untreated humans only then

$$
z(\tau) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{n\nu(0) - \tau\nu(\tau)}}
$$

where the growth rate $\nu$ depends on $\tau$ accounting for the fact it gets reduced
by any blood meal taken on treated patients and $n$ is the EIP in absence of treatment.
By definition, the EIP $T$ is the mean time post infection at which the parasite
reaches maturity for transmission, thus implicitly defined as

$$
z(T) = \frac{1}{2}.
$$
We can verify that, in absence of treatment (i.e. $\nu(\tau) = \nu(0)$, $\forall\tau$),
$z(n) = 1/2$.


#### 1 bite, all human treated

Call $\gamma(t, \tau)$ the **reduction factor of the maturation rate** consecutively to
1 blood meal at times $t$ and $\tau$. The mean reduction factor $q(\tau,m)$ of the
maturation rate across the population of infected mosquitoes due to
**1 bite on treated people at time $\tau$** then reads

$$
q(\tau,m) = \int_0^{m} \gamma(t, \tau) h(t) dt
$$


#### Multiple bites, $p\%$ human treated

In a similar way as done above for the parasite load, we can express the fact that each
bite on treated human reduces the maturation rate by $(1 - q(\tau,m))$% by the following
differential equation

$$
\frac{d\nu}{d\tau} = -(1 - q(\tau,m))ap(m)\nu(\tau,m)
$$

which leads to the following expression of the mean cumulative reduction factor of the
maturation rate:

$$
\kappa(\tau,m) = \exp\left[-ap(m) \int_0^\tau (1-q(s,m))\,ds\right]
$$

Now that we have this, we can implicitly express the average EIP $T$ in presence of the
treatment in the human population as the value $T$ satisfying 

$$
T\kappa(T,m) = n
$$

### $R_0$ reduction effect

Putting previous results together, if $R_0$ is the value of the basic reproduction
number in absence of treatment, then, in the presence of treatment in the population,
its expression becomes

$$
\theta e^{-(T - n)\mu} R_0
$$


## Experimental data

Let's use the following 4-parameter functional relationship for $\alpha(t, \tau)$,
$\beta(t, \tau)$ and $\gamma(t, \tau)$:

$$
f(t,\tau) = A \cdot (1 - e^{-kt})\cdot e^{-(dt + r\tau)}
$$

whereby, as function of $t$, the drug effects are characterized by an initial
saturating increase (captured by $k$) followed by an exponential decrease (captured by
$d$) reflecting the PK/PD of the drug and, as function of $\tau$, the effect is
characterized by an exponential decrease (captured by $r$) simply reflecting the growth
of the parasite (and thus the decrease of the relative concentration of the drug in
each blood meal). Parameter $A$ account for the maximum value reached.

A version of the model at 4 dpi:

```{r}
f4dpi <- function(t, A, k, d) A * (1 - exp(-k * t)) * exp(-d * t)
```

A function that looks for initial values at 4 dpi:

```{r}
initial_values <- function(x, y) {
  df <- tibble(x, y) |> 
    arrange(x)

  df2 <- df |> 
    group_by(x) |> 
    summarise(y = mean(y))
  
  A <- df2 |> 
    pull(y) |> 
    max()
  
  xs <- df2 |> 
    filter(y == A) |> 
    pull(x)

  k <- df |> 
    filter(x < first(xs)) |> 
    lm(y ~ -1 + x, data = _) |> 
    coef() |> 
    last()
  
  d <- df |>
    filter(x > last(xs)) |> 
    filter(y > 0) |> 
    mutate(across(y, log)) |> 
    lm(y ~ x, data = _) |> 
    coef() |> 
    last()
  
  c(A = A, k = k / A, d = -d)
}
```

A function that calibrates the model at 4 dpi with least sum of squares:

```{r}
calibrate4dpi <- function(x, y) {
  optim(initial_values(x, y), function(p) sum((y - f4dpi(x, p[1], p[2], p[3]))^2))$par
}
```


### $\alpha(t,\tau)$

Below, we generate the function $\alpha(t)$ from the experimental data of Figure 2a.
First we need a function that reads experimental data for the treatment group:

```{r}
alpha_data <- reading_exp_data("figure2a.rds")
```

Fitting the model to the data at 4 dpi:

```{r}
alpha_fit4dpi <- with(alpha_data, calibrate4dpi(t, value))
```

```{r}
make_effect <- function(A, k, d, r) {
  A <- A * exp(4 * 24 * r)
  function(t, tau) pmin(1, A * (1 - exp(-k * t)) * exp(-d * t - r * tau))
}
```

```{r}
alpha1 <- with(as.list(alpha_fit4dpi), make_effect(A, k, d, d))
```

```{r}
alpha2 <- with(as.list(alpha_fit4dpi), make_effect(A, k, d, d / 3))
```

```{r}
alpha <- alpha2
```

```{r fig.width = 4, fig.height = 4}
#| layout-ncol: 2
n_tau <- 10
n_t <- 100
t <- seq(0, 350, le = n_t)
tau <- seq(0, 350, le = n_tau)
tau_val <- 4 * 24

plot3d <- function(f) {
  opar <- par(plt = c(.05, .95, .05, .95))
  pmat <- expand_grid(t, tau) |> 
    mutate(value = f(t, tau)) |> 
    pull(value) |>
    matrix(n_tau) |> 
    persp(tau, t, z = _, theta = 45, border = 4, zlim = 0:1,
          xlab = "\u03C4 days post infection",
          ylab = "t days post drug administration",
          zlab = "TBA \u03B1")
  
  trans3d(rep(tau_val, n_t), t, alpha(t, tau_val), pmat) |> 
    with(lines(x, y, col = "red", lwd = 3))
  par(opar)
}

plot3d(alpha)
plot3d(alpha1)
```

```{r}
t_max <- 700
t_val <- 0:t_max

plot2d <- function(f) {
  plot(t_val, f(t_val, tau = 0), type = "n", ylim = 0:1,
       xlab = "time post drug administration (hours)",
       ylab = bquote("reduction" ~ alpha ~ "of mosquitoes with oocysts"))
  walk(seq(0, 700, 24), ~ lines(t_val, f(t_val, tau = .x), col = 4))
  lines(t_val, f(t_val, tau = 4 * 24), col = 2, lwd = lwd_val)
}

plot2d(alpha)
plot2d(alpha1)
```

A function that does bootstrapped calibration at 4 dpi:

```{r}
boot_calibration_4dpi <- function(data, N = 1e4, eps = 1.1) {
  model <- data |> 
    stratified_bootstrap(eps * N) |> 
    map(~ with(.x, safely(calibrate4dpi)(t, value)))

  model[map_lgl(model, ~ is.null(.x$error))] |>
    map("result") |> 
    sample(N)
}
```

It takes (1'20" on the laptop):

```{r eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
alpha_model_4dpi <- boot_calibration_4dpi(alpha_data)
```

```{r include = FALSE}
if (file_exists("alpha_model.rds")) {
  alpha_model_4dpi <- readRDScache("alpha_model.rds")
} else {
  alpha_model_4dpi <- boot_calibration_4dpi(alpha_data)
  saveRDScache(alpha_model_4dpi, "alpha_model.rds")
}
```

```{r}
t_val2 <- seq(0, 1.05 * t_max)

trajectories <- function(model, xs = t_val2) {
  model |> 
    set_names() |> 
    map_dfc(~ with(as.list(.x), f4dpi(xs, A, k, d)))
}
```

```{r}
alpha_trajectories <- trajectories(alpha_model_4dpi)
```

```{r}
plot_data_model <- function(data, simulations, ylabel, col_data = 4, col_model = 2) {
  with(data, plot(t, value, type = "n",
                  xlim = c(0, t_max), ylim = c(min(data$value), 1),
                  xlab = "time post drug administration (hours)",
                  ylab = ylabel))
  abline(h = 0)
  
  simulations |> 
    t() |> 
    as.data.frame() |> 
    map_dfr(quantile, c(.025, .5, .975)) |> 
    with({
      polygon2(t_val2, `2.5%`, `97.5%`, col = adjustcolor(col_model, .1))
      lines(t_val2, `50%`, lwd = lwd_val, col = col_model)
    })
  
  with(data, points(jitter(t), value, col = col_data, lwd = lwd_val, pch = 3))
}
```

```{r}
                bquote("reduction" ~ alpha ~ "of mosquitoes with oocysts"))
```

### $\zeta(\lambda)$

Here we are computing the function $\mu$ that converts a reduction in oocyst load into
a reduction in infectiousness. 

```{r message = FALSE}
bompard2020 <- "doi_10_5061_dryad_9p8cz8wfh__v20210123/act2datasetRpcr.txt" |>
  read_table2()
```

```{r}
bompard2020 |> 
  filter(0 < Total, Total < 50) |> 
  with(hist(Total, 0:50, xlab = "oocyst load L", ylab = "frequency",
            main = NA, col = 4))
```

```{r}
bompard2020 |> 
  group_by(Total) |> 
  tally() |> 
  mutate(cum_n = cumsum(n) / sum(n)) |> 
  with(plot(Total, cum_n, type = "h", col = 4, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(.85, 1),
            xlab = "oocyst load L", ylab = "cumulative proportion of samples"))
```

```{r}
weights <- bompard2020 |> 
  filter(Total > 0) |> 
  group_by(Total) |> 
  tally() |> 
  mutate(cum_n = cumsum(n) / sum(n)) |> 
  with(approx(Total, cum_n, 1:max(Total))) |> 
  setNames(c("load", "weight")) |> 
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(across(weight, ~ c(.x[1], diff(.x))))
```

Figure 2B from @aleshnick_experimental_2020 suggests a non-linear relationship $h$
between the sporozoite load and the transmission efficiency $b$ of *P. yoelii* from
*An. stephensi* mosquito to mice with 10,000 salivary gland sporozoites being
significantly more likely to initiate a malaria infection. Furthermore, Figure 1 from
@miura_strong_2019 documents a strong linear relationship between the numbers of
*P. falciparum* oocysts at 8 dpi and sporozoites at 16 dpi in *An. stephensi*
mosquitoes with about 1,000 sporozoites per oocyst (966, 95\% CI: 893–1038)).

Let's load the data from Figure 2B of @aleshnick_experimental_2020 on the relationship
between sporozoite load and the proportion of successful infections, converting it
into a relationship with oocyst load using @miura_strong_2019's 1000 factor.

```{r}
aleshnick2020 <- "ppat.1008181.s006.xlsx" |> 
  read_excel2() |> 
  mutate(load = `Salivary Gland Load` / 1000) |> 
  rename(infection = `Malaria Infection`) |> 
  select(load, infection)
```

A 2-parameter exponential saturating function of the probability of transmission as a
function of the parasite load:

$$
g(L) = B\cdot (1 - e^{-sL})
$$

```{r}
g <- function(L, B, s) B * (1 - exp(-s * L))
```

```{r}
th <- 25

B <- aleshnick2020 |> 
  filter(load > th) |> 
  pull(infection) |> 
  mean()

s <- aleshnick2020 |> 
  filter(load < th) |> 
  arrange(load) |> 
  map(~ zoo::rollmean(.x, 10)) |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  lm(infection ~ -1 + load, data = _) |> 
  coef()

mLL <- function(x) {
  -sum(with(aleshnick2020, dbinom(infection, 1, g(load, exp(x[1]), exp(x[2])), TRUE)))
}

params <- exp(optim(c(B = log(B), s = log(s)), mLL)$par)
g_calibrated <- function(x) g(x, params[1], params[2])
```

```{r}
max_load <- 250
load_vals <- 1:max_load

plot(load_vals, g_calibrated(load_vals), type = "h", lwd = lwd_val, col = 4,
     xlim = c(0, max_load), ylim = c(0, .5),
     xlab = "oocyst load L", ylab = "probability of transmission")
```

$$
\zeta(\lambda) = \sum_{L = 1}^{+\infty}\frac{g(\lambda L)}{g(L)}\omega(L)
$$

```{r}
zeta <- function(lambda, w = weights) {
  lambda |> 
    map_dbl(~ with(w, sum(weight * g_calibrated(.x * load) / g_calibrated(load))))
}
```

```{r}
lambda_vals <- seq(0, 1, le = 512)
zeta_vals <- zeta(lambda_vals)
```

```{r fig.height = eps * 5, fig.width = eps * 5, margin1 = FALSE, margin2 = TRUE}
#| label: fig-b_reduction
#| fig-cap: the conversion of a reduction on the sporozoite load $L$ into a reduction of the mosquito-to-human probability of transmission $b$ and $R_0$.

opar <- par(pty = "s", xpd = TRUE, plt = c(.15, .95, .15, .95))
plot(lambda_vals, zeta_vals, type = "l", lwd = lwd_val, col = 4,
     xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
     xlab = bquote("reducing factor of oocyst load"),
     ylab = "reducing factor of transmission")
segments(0, 0, 1, 1)
box(bty = "o")
par(opar)
```


### $\lambda(\tau)$

```{r}
integrate2 <- function(...) integrate(...)$value
```

```{r}
l <- function(tau, m) {
  map_dbl(tau,
          ~ integrate2(function(x) (1 - alpha(x, .x)) * (1 - beta(x, .x)), 0, m) / m)
}

# l(5:6 * 24, 15 * 24)
```

```{r}
lambda <- function(tau, a, p, m) {
  map_dbl(tau, ~ exp(-a * p * integrate2(function(x) 1 - l(x, m), 0, .x)))
}

# lambda(5:6 * 24, 1 / (3 * 24), 1, 50 * 24)
# zeta(lambda(5:6 * 24, 1 / (3 * 24), 1, 50 * 24))
```


### $\theta(\alpha, \beta)$

```{r}
theta <- function(mu, a, p, m, infinity) {
  integrate2(function(x) dexp(x, mu) * zeta(lambda(x, a, p, m)), 0, infinity)
}

# theta(mu = 1 / (14 * 24), a = 1 / (3 * 24), p = 1, m = 50 * 24, infinity = 50 * 24)
```

```{r include = FALSE}
  saveRDScache(delta_model_4dpi, "delta_model.rds")
}
```

```{r}

```

```{r}
                bquote("reduction" ~ delta ~ "of the size of oocysts"))
```

Estimating the EIPs with confidence intervals, forcing the same intercept at 3 dpi for

First, generating the models for each of the 4 combinations:

```{r}

  mutate(across(`Blood Feeds`, as.factor),
         time = `Days pIBM` - second_meal) |>
  summarise(mod = list(glm(infected ~ time + time:`Blood Feeds`, binomial)),
```

A function that adds proportion data with confidence interval to a plot:

```{r}
add_data <- function(x) {
  x |> 
    summarise(prop = list(prop.test(sum(infected), length(infected))),
              .by = c(`Days pIBM`, color)) |> 
    mutate(p  = map_dbl(prop, "estimate"),
           ci = map(prop, ~ setNames(.x$conf.int, c("lwr", "upr")))) |> 
    unnest_wider(ci) |> 
    with({
      col <- unique(color)
      points(`Days pIBM`, p, pch = 19, col = col)
      arrows2(`Days pIBM`, lwr, `Days pIBM`, upr, col = col)
    })
}
```

A function that finds the EIP from a given model and a given number of blood feeds:

```{r}
find_EIP <- function(mod, bf, val = "fit") {
  optimise(
    function(x) abs(predict_glm(mod, list(time = x, `Blood Feeds` = bf))[[val]] - .5),
    c(5, 20)
  )$min
}
```

```{r}
}
```


A function that converts a reduction in size into a reduction in rate:

```{r}
m_oo_size_val <- mean(oocyst_size_crtl)

size2rate_reduction <- function(reduction_in_size, ref = m_oo_size_val) {
  compute_rate(reduction_in_size * ref) / compute_rate(ref)
}

#size2rate_reduction(c(.8, .7))
#size2rate_reduction(0)
```

```{r}
qf <- function(tau, m) {
  map_dbl(tau,
          ~ integrate2(function(x) size2rate_reduction(1 - delta(x, .x)), 0, m) / m)
}

# qf(5:6 * 24, 15 * 24)
```

```{r}
kappaf <- function(tau, a, p, m) {
  map_dbl(tau, ~ exp(-a * p * integrate2(function(x) 1 - qf(x, m), 0, .x)))
}

# kappaf(5:6 * 24, 1 / (3 * 24), .1, 50 * 24)
```

```{r}
EIPf <- function(n, a, p, m) {
  optimise(function(x) abs(x * kappaf(x, a, p, m) - n), c(0, 24 * 100))$min
}

# EIPf(10 * 24, 1 / (3 * 24), .1, 50 * 24)
```

```{r}
reduction <- function(n, mu, a, p, m, infinity) {
  theta(mu, a, p, m, infinity) * exp((n - EIPf(n, a, p, m)) * mu)  
}

# reduction(10 * 24, 1 / (14 * 24), 1 / (3 * 24), .1, 50 * 24, 50 * 24)
```

## Explorations

### Mass treatment

A function that computes the $R_0$ reduction values in the context of mass treatment:

```{r}
mass_treatment <- function(n = 10, mu = 1 / 14, a = 1 / 3,
                           T_min = 3, T_max = 8, p_vals = 0:10 / 10, infinity = 250) {
  n <- n * 24
  mu <- mu / 24
  a <- a / 24
  infinity <- infinity * 24
  
  expand_grid(p_vals, m_vals = (T_min * 7):(T_max * 7) * 24) |> 
    mutate(reduction =
             future_map2_dbl(p_vals, m_vals,
                             ~ reduction(n, mu, a, p = .x, m = .y, infinity)))
}
```

A function that plots the output of `mass_treatment()`:

```{r}
plot_mass_treatment <- function(data) {
  with(data, plot(m_vals, reduction, type = "n", xaxt = "n", xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
                  xlab = "intake frequency (/week)",
                  ylab = bquote(R[0] ~ "reduction factor"),
                  xlim = rev(range(m_vals)), ylim = 0:1))
  
  hours_per_week <- 7 * 24
  T_range <- range(data$m_vals) / hours_per_week
  labels <- T_range[1]:T_range[2]
  ats <- labels * hours_per_week
  axis(1, ats, labels)
  abline(v = ats, col = "grey")
  abline(h = 0:10 / 10, col = "grey")
  
  data |> 
    group_split(p_vals) |> 
    walk2(YlOrRd11, ~ with(.x, lines(m_vals, reduction, col = .y, lwd = lwd_val)))
  
  box(bty = "o")
}
```

Takes 1':

```{r eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
plan(sequential)
```

```{r include = FALSE}
} else {
```

### Treatment of infected

The equilibrium proportion $\bar{S}$ of susceptible (to clinical infection) in the
population:

$$
\bar{S} = \frac{1 + ac/\mu}{R_0 + ac/\mu}
$$

where $c$ is the efficiency of transmission from human to mosquito. R code:

```{r}
susceptible <- function(R0, c, a, mu) {
  tmp <- a * c / mu
  (1 + tmp) / (R0 + tmp)
}
```

The proportion of susceptibles that gets a clinical infection over the past period of
time $m$:

$$
P_m = 1 - \exp\left(-\frac{(R_0-1)}{1+ac/\mu}rm\right)
$$

where $r$ is the human recovery rate. R code:

```{r}
proba_infection <- function(R0, r, m, a, c, mu) {
  1 - exp(-r * m * (R0 - 1) / (1 + a * c / mu))
}
```

Combining the two to compute the proportion of clinical cases over the past period of
time $m$:

$$
P_m\bar{S} = \frac{1+ac/\mu}{R_0+ac/\mu} \left[1-\exp\left(-\frac{(R_0-1)}{1+ac/\mu}rm\right)\right]
$$

R code:

```{r}
incidence <- function(R0, c, a, mu, r, m)  {
  tmp1 <- a * c / mu
  tmp2 <- tmp1 + 1
  tmp2 * (1 - exp(-r * m * (R0 - 1) / tmp2)) / (R0 + tmp1)
}
```

A function that shows the 3 things as a function of $R_0$: proportion of susceptibles,
probability of getting clinical infection and proportion of clinical infections:

```{r}
clinical_cases <- function(a = 1 / 3, mu = 1 / 14, r = 1 / 200, m = 30, c = .3) {
  R0s <- seq(1, 100, le = 512)
  prop_susc <- map_dbl(R0s, ~ susceptible(.x, c, a, mu))
  p_inf <- map_dbl(R0s, ~ proba_infection(.x, r, m, a, c, mu))
  plot(R0s, prop_susc, type = "l", lwd = lwd_val, col = 4,
       xlab = bquote(R[0]), ylab = "proportion or probability")
  lines(R0s, p_inf, lwd = lwd_val, col = 3)
  lines(R0s, p_inf * prop_susc, lwd = lwd_val, col = 2)
  legend("right", legend = c("proportion of susceptibles",
                             "probability of getting severely infected",
                             "proportion of clinical cases"),
         lty = 1, lwd = lwd_val, col = 4:2, bty = "n")
}
```

An example where incidence is defined over the past 30 days:

```{r}
clinical_cases(m = 30)
```

Zoom onto the incidence of clinical cases:

```{r}
R0s <- seq(1, 100, le = 512)
m <- 30
inc_vals <- map_dbl(R0s, ~ incidence(.x, c = .3, a = 1 / 3, mu = 1 / 14,
                                     r = 1 / 200, m = m))
plot(R0s, inc_vals, type = "l", lwd = lwd_val, col = 2,
     xlab = bquote(R[0]), ylab = paste("new clinical cases over the past", m, "days"))
```

A function that computes the iterations through the $R_0$ and $m$ values:

```{r}
dynamics <- function(R0i = 40, n = 10, mu = 1 / 14, a = 1 / 3, prop = 1, m = 50,
                     cv = .3, r = 1 / 200, infinity = 250, nb = 10) {
  R0 <- p <- rep(0, nb + 1)
  R0 <- R0_tmp <- R0i
  for (i in 2:(nb + 1)) {
    p[i - 1] <- p_tmp <- incidence(R0_tmp, cv, a, mu, r, m)
    R0[i] <- R0_tmp <- reduction(n, mu, a, prop * p_tmp, m, infinity) * R0i
  }
  list(R0 = R0, p = head(p, -1))
}
```

A function that draws the outpout of `dynamics()`:

```{r}
plot_dynamics <- function(x) {
  plott <- function(...) {
    plot(..., type = "o", xlab = "iteration", col = 4, lwd = lwd_val)
  }
  with(x, {
    plott(R0, ylab = bquote(R[0]))
    plott(p,  ylab = "incidence")
  })
}
```

Computing the dynamics of starting values of $R_0$ of 40 and 30:

```{r eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
out40 <- dynamics()
out30 <- dynamics(30)
```

```{r include = FALSE}
if (file_exists("out40.rds")) {
  out40 <- readRDScache("out40.rds")
} else {
  out40 <- dynamics()
  saveRDScache(out40, "out40.rds")
}

if (file_exists("out30.rds")) {
  out30 <- readRDScache("out30.rds")
} else {
  out30 <- dynamics()
  saveRDScache(out30, "out30.rds")
}
```

Through manual iterations we can see that a limit cycle appears for `R0i` below 40:

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
plot_dynamics(out40)
plot_dynamics(out30)
```

A function that looks for the equilibrium value of $R_0$ using the `nleqslv` package:

```{r}
finalR0nl <- function(R0i, n, mu, a, prop, m, cv, r, infinity = 250) {
  nleqslv::nleqslv(c(R0i, incidence(R0i, cv, a, mu, r, m)),
                   function(vars) {
                      R0 <- vars[1]
                      p  <- vars[2]
                      c(R0 - reduction(n, mu, a, prop * p, m, infinity) * R0i,
                        p  - incidence(R0, cv, a, mu, r, m)) })$x[1]
}
```

A function that does the same but using the `rootSolve` package:

```{r}
finalR0rs <- function(R0i, n, mu, a, prop, m, cv, r, infinity = 250) {
  rootSolve::multiroot(function(vars) {
                         R0 <- vars[1]
                         p  <- vars[2]
                         c(R0 - reduction(n, mu, a, prop * p, m, infinity) * R0i,
                           p  - incidence(R0, cv, a, mu, r, m)) },
                       c(R0i, incidence(R0i, cv, a, mu, r, m)))$root[1]
}
```

The functions from the `nleqslv` and `rootSolve` packages are equivalent but `nleqslv`
is slightly faster. Explorations:

(takes 8'40" in sequential mode on the Mac Mini and 24" in parallel mode on the M2)

```{r eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
                                                        a = 1 / 3, prop = 1, m = .y,
                                                        cv = .3, r = 1 / 200) / .x))
```

Let's try to perform Hill extrapolation for each value of `prop` and get rid off all
the `prop` values where extrapolation fails. We e

```{r}
tmp <- R0red2 |> 
  summarise(fit = list(safely(nls)(reduction ~ R0^h / (K^h + R0^h),
                                   data = pick(everything()),
                                   start = c(K = 5, h = .7))), .by = prop) |> 
  filter_out(map_lgl(map(fit, "result"), is.null)) |> 
  mutate(across(fit, ~ map(.x, "result")),
         coeff = map(fit, coef)) |>
  unnest_wider(coeff)

modK <- tmp |> 
  select(prop, K) |> 
  bind_rows(tibble(prop = 0, K = 0)) |> 
  lm(K ~ prop + I(prop^2), data = _)

modh <- lm(h ~ prop + I(prop^2), tmp)

out <- R0red2 |> 
  nest(.by = prop) |>
  mutate(K0  = predict(modK, list(prop = prop)),
         h0  = predict(modh, list(prop = prop)),
         fit = pmap(list(data, K0, h0),
                    ~ nls(reduction ~ R0^h / (K^h + R0^h),
                          data = ..1, start = c(K = ..2, h = ..3))),
         reduction = map(fit,
                         ~ tibble(R0 = R0_new,
                                  prediction = predict(.x,
                                                       newdata = list(R0 = R0_new))))) |> 
  select(-c(K0, h0, fit))
```

Verifying the quality of the extrapolations:

```{r}
out |>

  unnest(reduction) |> 
  group_by(prop) |> 
  group_walk(~ with(.x, lines(R0, prediction, col = 4)))

out |> 
  select(prop, data) |> 
  unnest(data) |> 
  group_by(prop) |> 
  group_walk(~ with(.x, points(R0, reduction, col = 4)))
```

```{r}
plot_treatment_infected <- function(data) {
  plot(NA, xlim = c(15, 150), ylim = 0:1, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
     xlab = bquote(initial ~ value ~ of ~ R[0]), ylab = bquote(R[0] ~ reduction))
  
  abline(v = 0:15 * 10, col = "grey")
  abline(h = 0:10 / 10, col = "grey")
  
  data |> 
    select(prop, reduction) |> 
    unnest(reduction) |> 
    group_split(prop) |> 
    walk2(tail(YlOrRd11, -1), ~ with(.x, lines(R0, prediction, col = .y, lwd = lwd_val)))
  
  box(bty = "o")
}

plot_treatment_infected(out)
```
